title: Best Developer Productivity Platforms for Engineering Teams (2026)
summary: Compare Weave, DX, Jellyfish, LinearB, and Swarmia for code output, AI ROI, quality, delivery benchmarks, and engineering investment reporting.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- **Weave is built for engineering teams that need output, quality, AI ROI, and investment reporting in one platform.** Silk 1 reads the code itself, while Engineering Intelligence and Token Intelligence connect that work to reviews, delivery, benchmarks, and cost.
- **The key comparison is how a platform measures work.** Counts of commits, PRs, and story points cannot distinguish a routine fix from a complex migration. Weave measures both on a common scale of expert engineering effort.
- DX combines developer experience research with productivity and AI analytics. Jellyfish focuses on engineering investment and AI Impact. LinearB combines analytics with workflow automation. Swarmia provides team-level feedback and AI cost reporting.


Weave publishes this guide. The product descriptions use the first-party sources linked below, reviewed October 6, 2026.


## What engineering leaders need from a productivity platform


A useful platform answers more than how busy your team is. It should show how much work shipped, how good that work is, where delivery slows down, and whether AI spending improves results.


DORA metrics remain useful for delivery speed and reliability. Pair them with code output, review quality, AI usage, and cost to understand the engineering organization as a whole. For investment decisions, connect the same data to projects, portfolios, and R&D capitalization.


## Weave: measure engineering work, quality, and AI impact


[Weave](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence) combines code analysis, engineering productivity, and AI intelligence. It gives engineers, managers, CTOs, and finance a shared view of output, quality, delivery, and investment.


### Understand the work inside every PR


[Silk 1](https://weaveos.com/products/code-intelligence) reads the full diff and reasons about intent, risk, complexity, and dependencies across files. Output is measured in the effort an expert engineer would need to complete the change, giving teams a common unit across people, repositories, and languages.


Every score includes a plain-language explanation. Team overrides feed organization-aware calibration. Silk 1 reports 3.3× lower average prediction error than its earlier model, with 88% of PR scores within ±1h of an expert estimate.


This is the distinction between counting work items and understanding the work: a short change that affects a large system can be more significant than a long, routine diff.


### Connect AI activity and spending to results


[Token Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence) tracks human and agent contributions, AI adoption, usage, and cost. Weave shows per-engineer costs where the connected tool provides that detail; less granular sources remain at the organization level. The report identifies provider-billed, usage-based, seat, and estimated costs so teams can distinguish invoice-backed spend from estimates.


Compare those costs with AI-attributable code output, review effort, code turnover, and delivery. Leaders can see which tools and workflows produce useful work, then use[Weave Router](https://weaveos.com/products/router) to optimize model selection inside coding agents.


### Find bottlenecks and support financial decisions


Engineering Intelligence measures review depth, rounds before merge, reverts, code churn, incident-to-PR links, and deployment performance. Benchmarks draw on real engineering data from thousands of organizations, segmented by organization size.


Weave also includes R&D capitalization, portfolio views, and[custom dashboards](https://weaveos.com/custom-dashboards) .[Wooly](https://weaveos.com/products/wooly) answers questions about engineering data, and[Weave Checks](https://weaveos.com/checks) runs automated checks on pull requests. Measurement, reporting, and action belong in the same engineering workflow.


## DX: developer experience research and productivity frameworks


[DX](https://getdx.com/) combines developer experience research, delivery analytics, and AI measurement. Its[AI cost management report](https://docs.getdx.com/reports/ai-cost-management/) tracks estimated spend, tokens, credits, and contributor breakdowns, with cost per PR calculated as estimated total cost divided by merged PRs.


DX requires Data Cloud and a supported AI source for this report. Its documentation says merged PRs and cost per PR are unavailable when filtering to a subset of AI tools. Compare that approach with Weave's code-based output measurement and person and tool cost reporting when evaluating AI investment.


Read the[Weave vs DX comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-dx) .


## Jellyfish: engineering investment and AI Impact


[Jellyfish](https://jellyfish.co/) combines engineering investment allocation with operational and AI reporting. Its[AI token cost management product](https://jellyfish.co/platform/jellyfish-ai-impact/ai-token-usage-monitoring/) compares token spending with throughput, forecasts, and budget allocation.


Financial reporting is also part of Weave. Weave's R&D capitalization analyzes PR output, task associations, and project data, while Silk 1 adds code-level complexity measurement and explainable scores to investment decisions.


Read the[Weave vs Jellyfish comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-jellyfish) .


## LinearB: delivery analytics and workflow automation


[LinearB](https://linearb.io/platform/overview) combines AI usage and impact measurement with code review and workflow automation. Its platform follows commit and review activity and helps teams act on delivery bottlenecks.


Weave adds complexity-aware output, review-depth analysis, code-quality signals, and AI costs to that delivery discussion. Weave Checks provides automated PR checks, while Wooly helps teams investigate their engineering data.


Read the[Weave vs LinearB comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-linearb) .


## Swarmia: team feedback and AI cost reporting


[Swarmia](https://www.swarmia.com/) provides engineering analytics and continuous team feedback. Its[AI ROI view](https://www.swarmia.com/changelog/2026-08-07-ai-roi/) combines an administrator-configured developer cost with the list price of consumed AI tokens, reporting cost per story, merged PR, or line changed.


Weave pairs AI costs with Silk 1's common output scale and engineering quality. Provider billing connections also let teams use actual billed spend where available, with the cost source visible in the report.


Read the[Weave vs Swarmia comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-swarmia) .

The difference is not simply whether a platform has an AI dashboard. It is whether its output unit captures the work inside a change and whether leaders can inspect cost, quality, and delivery together.


## How to choose a developer productivity platform


Start with the question your team needs to answer, then inspect the data behind it.


- **Engineering productivity:** read the output score and explanation for a feature, a bug fix, and a refactor. Check whether the platform recognizes their different scope and complexity.
- **AI investment:** compare spend by person and tool with output and quality over a consistent period.
- **Delivery improvement:** inspect review cycles, revert rates, deployment performance, and the work behind a bottleneck.
- **Finance and leadership:** use R&D capitalization, portfolio views, and shared dashboards to connect work with investment.


Weave covers all four in one platform, with a consistent code-output measure underneath the reports. Connect your repositories and AI tools, inspect real PRs, and use your team's questions to guide the evaluation.

## FAQs


### What makes Weave different from a DORA dashboard?


DORA measures delivery mechanics. Weave also analyzes the code inside every PR, measures output and quality, attributes AI contributions, and connects spending with engineering results.


### Can Weave help with R&D capitalization?


Yes. Weave analyzes PR output, task associations, and project data to identify development work for capitalization. Reports can be broken down by team, repository, or project.


### Does Weave measure individual and team performance?


Yes. Weave reports output and quality at individual and team levels, with a common scoring scale, context for the work, and explanations behind the scores.


### Does Weave support GitHub and GitLab?


Weave connects to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and Gerrit. Confirm the connection and deployment requirements for your repositories during setup.


### How does Weave benchmark engineering teams?


Weave uses engineering data from thousands of organizations, with size-based segments and benchmarks for output per engineer, reviews, and delivery performance.
